observations.summary: The child filter can match nothing without anyone noticing: libtest exits 0 when an --exact filter selects no test, so a rename or module move that leaves the hard-coded name string behind makes the child run nothing and the parent pass (V1N1: the r3 ordering then passes). One parent-side line closes it (H1N1 killed, H1 no false alarm): assert_eq!(fs::metadata(f.0.join("umaskdir")).unwrap().mode() & 0o777, 0o700); or check the child's stdout for '1 passed'. The gap was also in the child-process shape the reviewer suggested at r4.

Coverage (carried from r4): of the r4 mutants, N4 errno ignored, N6 scan call removed, N7 owner-uid test removed and N8 closedir skipped on error are killed only by reviewer probes; N5 owner check removed by none (race only); N3 errno not cleared is killed by owner tests (measured at r4 on byte-identical production code).

Carried from r3/r4: link count 2 is a filesystem convention (APFS counts every entry; btrfs reports 1, fail-closed); identity not proven for a same-owner empty directory (acceptable); create_exclusive_directory's doc does not mention the refusal or the scan-after-mode order; the fstat buffer is not counted in bytes.
The child's second umask call and close(scan) lack SAFETY comments; one SAFETY comment covers two cfg-selected unsafe blocks in clear_errno/current_errno.

descriptor_filesystem::tests::native_filesystem_original_file_lock_and_all_path_components_stay_owned fails 3-7% of parallel runs (ChangedDuringRead), on the base as well; a single run of the requested --test-threads=8 command can fail for this unrelated reason. Out of scope.

Security test lacks directory existing-entry/symlink cases; single_component error text says 'file'; residual entry after refusal and retry AlreadyExists; public unaccounted create_exclusive_*; openat mode style nit; unused From impls and nested WorkFailure.
